text: Android: self-hosted TLS reality — indistinct error messages, self-signed certs unsupported

relates: T-46 — complementary solutions to the same self-signed-dev-cert
problem. T-46 is a debug-only trust-ALL bypass flag (quick dev path, forced off
in release); this ticket's networkSecurityConfig trusting user-installed CAs is
the "proper" self-host path that also works in release. Whoever picks up either
should know the other exists; ideally the distinct SSLException message here
points the user at both options (install your CA, or flip the dev flag).

Done in 0e2a23d. SSLException caught distinctly (before IOException, which it
subclasses) in LoginViewModel.submit AND SyncEngine (surfaces "Server certificate
not trusted" into the T-47 sync-health lastError). res/xml/network_security_config
.xml trusts system + user-installed CAs (release-safe self-host path), referenced
from the manifest; cleartext stays off. android/README documents all three options
and the message points at them. Ties to T-46 (note#1): T-46 is the debug-only
trust-all flag; this is the proper release path — the error text mentions both.
Test: SSLHandshakeException -> distinct cert message. Note: the actual cert-trust
behavior (user CA install, self-signed handshake) is on-device only; unit test
covers the message branch.

Follow-up in the login commit above (on-device finding): the T-46 self-signed
toggle was only in Settings, which is unreachable until you're logged in — a
bootstrap deadlock for a self-signed server. Surfaced the same debug-gated toggle
on the login screen (ApiProvider rebuilds its client on the flag, so flip-and-retry
works without a restart). Release builds unaffected (BuildConfig.DEBUG + no-op
DevCertTrust). Tests + lint green; APK rebuilt for the device pass.
